notes: Machine-readable SKU map for the nutrition mechanic. `id` is the stable key referenced by NutritionLog.during[].skuId in src/core/types.ts.
Every numeric field is per SINGLE SERVING as defined by `servingNote`, not per 100 g.
sodiumMg is derived from the on-pack `salt` figure using the EU convention sodium = salt / 2.5, except where the pack prints a sodium figure directly (Isotonic Drink, Salt Caps) — see sourceNote.

verified=true means the number was read off a primary source: an Enervit packaging artwork / ingredient panel in the local brand-asset library, or an enervit.com product page. verified=false means the number is derived, rounded, from a secondary source, or internally inconsistent — DO NOT put a verified=false number in player-facing copy without client sign-off.
packshotPath is absolute. `traspa` = transparent background, preferred for UI compositing.
phase follows Enervit's own NUTRITION SYSTEM® placement. Products usable in more than one phase carry `alsoPhase`.
See NUTRITION_PROTOCOL.md for the phase timings and CLAIMS_TO_REVIEW.md before writing any player-facing copy about these products.

nameCz values were read from eshop.enervit.cz and enervitshop.cz, the official Enervit CZ/SK shops operated by the distributor VITAR Sport s.r.o. IMPORTANT: the Czech market does NOT translate SKU names — products are sold under the English brand name with an 'ENERVIT' prefix, and only flavours and pack descriptors are Czech. nameCz is therefore a prefix+suffix transformation, not a translation. Flavour spellings and pack sizes carry transcription risk and should be spot-checked against the live shop before shipping. A null nameCz means the name could NOT be found and must not be guessed.

nameCz MUST BE UNIQUE across SKUs. The runtime renders it as the sole product label (skuLabel() in src/race/hud.ts prefers nameCz, and src/ui/beforeScreen.ts uses it for the loadout cards), so two SKUs sharing a nameCz are two visually identical cards the player cannot tell apart. Where the shops sell several flavours under one base name, carry the flavour in nameCz using the base+en-dash+flavour form — 'ENERVIT Carbo Gel C2:1 – pomeranč'. Re-checked 2026-08-02: the six then-colliding names were resolved from live listings, and the map's earlier belief that the Czech shops list gels only as 'mix příchutí' bundles is out of date — every flavour now has its own product page. The two shops sometimes disagree on capitalisation and on whether the flavour appears at all ('Enervit gel - cola' vs 'ENERVIT Gel'), and they use a plain hyphen; nameCz normalises to the 'ENERVIT' prefix and the en dash for consistency, but the flavour word itself is always transcribed, never invented or translated.

gameStat.focus is 0.0 for EVERY SKU by design, not by omission. No product may drive the focus stat — see CLAIMS_TO_REVIEW.md §3.1 and §5. This is a compliance boundary, not a balance decision: do not 'fix' it.

gameStat values are design starting points, not measurements. Only the carbsG/sodiumMg/caffeineMg/proteinG fields carry sourced data. Any player-facing statement derived from a gameStat must clear CLAIMS_TO_REVIEW.md first.

skus.packshotPath: /Users/jurajgiacko/Projects/JG 2026/VitarSport2026/Context/brand-assets/enervit-brand/C2_1/ISOCARB/Enervit barattolo alto 168,5 X 214 Isocarb 2022 traspa.png
skus.sourceNote: PRIMARY: on-pack panel C2_1/ISOCARB/Ingredienti isocarb.jpg. Per 65 g dose in 500 ml: 244 kcal, 60 g carbohydrate, 20 g sugars, 0.6 g salt (→ 240 mg sodium), thiamine 0.41 mg. Ingredients: maltodextrin DE1 AgenaNova 66%, fructose 31% (= 2.1:1), citric acid, sodium chloride, natural lemon flavour, thiamine hydrochloride. COMPLIANCE FLAG: at 60 g carbohydrate in 500 ml this is ~488 kcal/l, which EXCEEDS the 350 kcal/l ceiling in the EU carbohydrate-electrolyte solution claim conditions. Isocarb therefore CANNOT carry those claims even though the Isotonic Drink can. See CLAIMS_TO_REVIEW.md.
skus.gameNote: A full hour of Long-race fuelling in one bottle. Hydration gain is deliberately lower than Isotonic Drink at the same 500 ml because the concentration is more than double — the same volume of water doing more carbohydrate work and less hydration work. That difference is the whole reason both SKUs exist, and it is a mechanic worth making visible. COMPLIANCE OVERRIDE: focus was zeroed. Per CLAIMS_TO_REVIEW.md no product in the range may drive the focus stat — there is no authorised EU cognition claim on any of these SKUs, and for caffeine there is no authorised claim of any kind (the Commission's draft was vetoed by the European Parliament, P8_TA(2016)0319). A product-driven focus effect would be a symbolic health claim under Art. 2(2)(1) of Reg. 1924/2006. Drive focus from fatigue and terrain only.

skus.sourceNote: From enervit.com (r2-recovery-drink-sachet.html and the tub page). Per 50 g dose: 188 kcal, 41 g carbohydrate, 2.9 g sugars, 4.4 g protein, 0.17 g salt (→ 68 mg sodium), vit E 10 mg, vit C 60 mg, thiamine 0.5 mg, riboflavin 1 mg, niacin 10 mg, vit B6 1 mg. The declared 4.4 g 'protein' is free amino acids (BCAA + glutamine), NOT intact protein — this matters, because the EU protein claims require protein to supply a set share of energy and 4.4 g against 188 kcal comes nowhere near it. R1 and R2 are clearly distinct products; whether 'Recovery Drink 400 g' is a third SKU is unresolved.

skus.sourceNote: PRIMARY: on-pack panel SPORT/MAGIC CHERRY/Immagine 6_MagicCherry-ingredienti.jpg. The panel declares only tart cherry extract (Prunus cerasus, Vistula variety, 26.7%) with polyphenols 300 mg and anthocyanins 50 mg per 9 g sachet, plus vitamin E 3.6 mg (30% NRV); 600 mg polyphenols / 100 mg anthocyanins / 7.2 mg vit E per 18 g. Macronutrients are NOT declared on this panel, hence carbsG null. COMPLIANCE FLAG: tart cherry polyphenols and anthocyanins have NO authorised EU health claim. Vitamin E's only authorised claim is protection of cells from oxidative stress — which is NOT a recovery, muscle-damage or soreness claim. This SKU is the single highest claims risk in the range.
skus.gameNote: Deliberately all zeros. Commercially this product is a CZ/SK success (first pallets sold out in days) so there will be pressure to give it a visible in-game effect — but there is no authorised claim to hang one on, and inventing a 'recovery' stat boost for it would be exactly the kind of implied health claim that gets a client in trouble. If it appears at all, it should be cosmetic or flavour-fatigue relief. Escalate to the client's regulatory contact before giving it any stat.
